SMTO-SKL-0170 — The pull request changed or has conflicts, so SMTO stopped

GUID: 676f460c-ff63-50f7-a970-7c8aae3c80cd
Slug: github-pull-head-changed
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: github

What happened

  • The pull request got new commits after you approved this, or GitHub reported a conflict. SMTO only merges or reviews the exact version you checked, so the pull request wasn't merged or reviewed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the pull request on github.com and look at its newest commits and whether it says there are conflicts. Something changed since you approved the action, and you should see what before going ahead.
  2. If GitHub shows conflicts, resolve them on github.com, or ask the person who opened the pull request to fix them. GitHub won't merge a pull request that conflicts with the branch it is going into.
  3. Review the new changes and their checks, then ask SMTO to merge or review again and confirm the latest version when asked. SMTO needs your approval for the exact version it acts on.

What success looks like

  • The pull request shows as merged, or your review appears on it on github.com.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't approve a version you haven't looked at just to get past this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The pull request's current head SHA differs from the confirmed expected_head_sha, or GitHub rejected the merge with HTTP 409 (head mismatch or merge conflict).

What this means

  • Merge receives HTTP 409, or pre-review/pre-merge readback finds a different head SHA from expected_head_sha. This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.

Why this can happen

  • Merge receives HTTP 409, or pre-review/pre-merge readback finds a different head SHA from expected_head_sha.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare exact current head SHA and the provider conflict response before concluding a specific commit changed.

How to fix it

  • Before pull_review/pull_merge, GitHubService.dispatch re-reads the PR and raises pull_head_changed if head.sha differs from expected_head_sha/commit_id; a merge PUT returning HTTP 409 maps to the same code. Read the current PR head, checks and conflict state, then obtain a new deliberate confirmation bound to the current head SHA.
  • Read the exact PR head and conflict detail, then obtain deliberate confirmation for the current intended commit.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • A deliberate new confirmation binds the intended current head after checks are reviewed.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
